subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should current global/agent exec security configuration act as a hard floor over persisted `/exec` session defaults, or should authorized per-session `/exec` overrides remain able to shadow later config until reset?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally preserve authorized session defaults, but the report shows that this can undermine later operator security tightening; automation cannot choose that security/compatibility tradeoff safely.

options.title: Make config a hard floor
options.body: Treat current global/agent/approval policy as the maximum allowed exec capability, keep `/exec` for equal-or-stricter session defaults, and add migration/reset coverage for stored weaker entries.

options.title: Keep session override contract
options.body: Document that `/exec` session defaults intentionally outlive config edits and direct operators to tool policy, host approvals, or session reset for hard revocation.

options.title: Add explicit reset without precedence change
options.body: Keep the current resolver order but add a visible operator command/doctor path to clear stale exec fields per session or channel.

recommendation.title: Make config a hard floor
recommendation.body: Treat current global/agent/approval policy as the maximum allowed exec capability, keep `/exec` for equal-or-stricter session defaults, and add migration/reset coverage for stored weaker entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The current `/exec` session override contract and resolver tests trace most directly to this history.
